_comment: Metafield definitions. Four of them, and each exists because something on a
page needs a fact that Shopify has no native field for.
EVERY DEFINITION IS PINNED. An unpinned definition is invisible in the admin
form, and the Girlyf team would reasonably conclude the feature is missing.
Pinning is not cosmetic here — it is the difference between a field they use
and a field they never find.
THE ORDER OF THIS LIST IS THE ORDER OF THE ADMIN FORM. Shopify pins in the
order definitions are created, so what decides where a product APPEARS comes
first (category, material), then how it SHIPS (pack size), then the optional
extras. A store that already had some of these will keep the old order — the
fix is unpin-all then repin in this order, and it is worth doing: category
sitting below `Reels` teaches the form wrong.
There are no metaobjects. Girlyf has no fact that two products would share
the identical text of — unlike Homingo, whose material and care copy is keyed
by material family. If that changes, a metaobject is the right answer, not a

definitions.name: Category
definitions.description: What this piece IS. Pick one. This is what puts the product on its category page — get it wrong and the product appears nowhere. Choose 'combo' for a boxed set of several pieces.
definitions._why: A choices validation renders as a DROPDOWN in the admin, so `earings` is not typeable. That is the guarantee the fill sheet used to provide and the tag autocomplete never did — a mistyped category tag saves cleanly and the product silently appears in no category page at all.
definitions._capability: smartCollectionCondition must be enabled or the category collections CANNOT be built on this field. The enum accepts PRODUCT_METAFIELD_DEFINITION regardless; the store rejects it unless the definition opts in.

definitions.name: Material
definitions.description: What it is made of. Pick one, or two for pieces that are genuinely both. Drives the storefront filters.
definitions._why: Same locked vocabulary as category, one stakes lower — a wrong material loses a filter match rather than a whole category page. A list type because a piece can honestly be two materials.

definitions.name: Specs
definitions.description: The trust facts, as a tick list under the description. Pick every one that is true. These are claims, so only tick what the piece actually is.
definitions._why: Every competitor leads with these: The Beige's product body is literally '18k gold plated / Stainless Steel / Water-resistant / Hypoallergenic / Anti-tarnish'. The brand guidelines ask for warm prose instead, and shoppers scan for both. A locked list gives the trust signals without 150 people retyping them 150 ways, and keeps the description free to be prose.
definitions._not_a_collection: Specs drive no collection and no rule. A shopper filters by material, not by hypoallergenic, so this stays a display fact.

definitions.name: Pack size
definitions.description: Which box this ships in. The owner picks; nobody measures. Weight goes in Shopify's own weight field, in grams.
definitions._why: Indian couriers bill on max(actual, volumetric). Jewellery is light, so actual weight almost always wins and per-product L×W×H would be four more fields to guess at. A named box keeps packing consistent and lets box→dimensions live in ONE table if a courier integration ever needs volumetric.
definitions._not_a_metafield: Weight itself is Shopify's native per-variant field. Duplicating it here would create two answers to one question.

definitions.name: Free size
definitions.description: Set by the fill-sheet importer, not by hand. True when a ring is adjustable rather than sized, and the theme renders it as a badge. Only rings answer this at all — a necklace leaves it blank.
definitions._why: The checklist asked for adjustable pieces to be 'labelled clearly to reduce returns'. A badge driven by data does that; words someone remembers to type into a title do not.

definitions.name: Reels
definitions.description: Styled vertical clips, usually repurposed from Instagram. These render in their own strip, deliberately NOT in the product media gallery. A worn/turning trust video belongs in the gallery instead — upload that as ordinary product media.
definitions._why: A 9:16 marketing clip sitting between two packshots makes the gallery incoherent. Different role, different surface.

definitions.name: Combo contains
definitions.description: The individual pieces inside a pre-packed combo. Lets the product page say what is in the box and link to each piece. Set this by hand, once per combo — the fill sheet lists handles, which are not Shopify references.
definitions._why: A combo without this is a mystery box with a photo. It is also the one field the sheet describes but cannot deliver.

definitions.name: Category tile clip
definitions.description: A 3–5 second loop standing in for this category's static tile image. Muted, no audio track, under 8MB, with a poster frame. One per category.
definitions._why: A Shopify collection has one image field and no video field, so the guidelines' looping category tiles are not expressible natively.
